b2-costarica-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Where Turtles Lay Eggs
b2-costarica-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are planning a trip to Costa Rica, and he asks you where the green turtles lay their eggs.
b2-costarica-01.prompt: Tell Carlos where the turtles lay their eggs, putting the place in the spotlight.
cues: Say what the turtles do there
b2-costarica-01.target: Es en Tortuguero, en la costa del Caribe, donde desovan las tortugas verdes.
b2-costarica-01.english: It is in Tortuguero, on the Caribbean coast, that the green turtles lay their eggs.
b2-costarica-01.canDo: I can put a place, a time or an idea in the spotlight with *Fue… donde / cuando* and *Lo que… es…*.

b2-costarica-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Country Without an Army
b2-costarica-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are watching a documentary about Costa Rica, and she asks you if the country has no security at all.
b2-costarica-02.prompt: Correct her idea and say who provides security.
b2-costarica-02.target: No es que Costa Rica no tenga seguridad, sino que no tiene ejército.
b2-costarica-02.english: It isn't that Costa Rica has no security; it's that it has no army.
b2-costarica-02.canDo: I can correct a reason with *No es que… sino que…*.

b2-costarica-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Fact That
b2-costarica-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading an article about the CCSS, and he asks you what challenge the health system has.
b2-costarica-03.prompt: Comment on the fact that the population is getting older.
b2-costarica-03.target: El hecho de que la población envejezca crea nuevos retos para la CCSS.
b2-costarica-03.english: The fact that the population is getting older creates new challenges for the CCSS.
b2-costarica-03.canDo: I can comment on a known fact with *el hecho de que* + subjunctive.

b2-costarica-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Before the Visitors Arrive
b2-costarica-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are planning a visit to a national park, and she asks what the guides do before the groups come.
b2-costarica-04.prompt: Tell Meg what the guides do and when.
cues: Say that they do it before the visitors arrive
b2-costarica-04.target: Los guías revisan los senderos antes de que lleguen los visitantes.
b2-costarica-04.english: The guides check the trails before the visitors arrive.
b2-costarica-04.canDo: I can say what happened before or after someone else's action, with *antes de que* and *después de que*.

b2-costarica-05.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Unions Want
b2-costarica-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading a report about pineapple farms in Costa Rica, and he asks you what the unions want.
b2-costarica-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what the unions want from the companies.
cues: Say what the companies should do
b2-costarica-05.target: Los sindicatos quieren que las empresas paguen el salario mínimo.
b2-costarica-05.english: The unions want the companies to pay the minimum wage.
b2-costarica-05.canDo: I can choose between an infinitive and *que* + subjunctive, depending on who does the second action.

b2-costarica-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Review: Costa Rica
b2-costarica-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are planning a trip to Costa Rica, and she asks what you remember about the country.
b2-costarica-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg one fact about nature and one about the army.
cues: Put what surprises you in the spotlight
Correct the idea that the country has no police
b2-costarica-consolidation.target: Lo que más sorprende en Costa Rica es la variedad de especies. No es que no tenga policía, sino que no tiene ejército.
b2-costarica-consolidation.english: What surprises most in Costa Rica is the variety of species. It is not that it has no police, but that it has no army.
b2-costarica-consolidation.canDo: I can put a place, a time or an idea in the spotlight with *Fue… donde* and *Lo que… es…*.
